analysis.title: US Market Intelligence Afternoon Briefing (November 2, 2026)
key_insights: US stocks closed mixed on Nov 2 (SPX +0.3%, NDX +0.5%, RTY +0.4%) as oil and bond yields fell on US/Iran deal optimism. Trump told reporters there are no plans to strike Iran after the elections. Tech failed to hold its pre-market bid and Memory and Semis reversed lower. AAPL fell about 1.5% after earnings.
JPM describes the price action as a continuation of October, with a rotation out of Tech and AI themes. Desk flows were quiet ahead of the midterms.

October ISM manufacturing: the production index rose 2.3 points to 59.0, its highest since November 2021. New orders rose 0.2 points to 55.5 and employment edged down to 52.4. The ISM prices paid index pulled back modestly but stayed near its second-highest level since March 2022.

The final S&P PMI showed input cost inflation at its highest since May and output price inflation at its strongest since September 2022. Supplier delivery times lengthened the most since August 2022. The release cites AI-related demand, tariffs and Middle East disruption. PMI employment growth was the strongest in nearly six years.

JPM Market Intel calls the ISM print a Goldilocks print, with growth accelerating and inflationary pressure moderating but still high. It thinks Tech was oversold but has not seen the all clear for AI and Tech, so the broadening trade (Cyclicals, SMid-Caps, Financials, Consumer) is where money should keep going.

Midterm scenario odds from JPM: Blue Wave (Dem House and Senate) 66%, Split Congress (Dem House, GOP Senate) 26%, Red Wave 7%, GOP House with Dem Senate 1%. Estimated SPX impact runs from -25bp to +50bp in a Blue Wave, up to +1.25% in a Red Wave.

In a Blue Wave, JPM argues AI regulation would be hard to pass because Trump has said he will not sign bills limiting AI expansion and Democrats cannot reach a veto-proof majority. The risks are de-grossing within the AI theme, and investigation risk for business leaders tied to Trump donations, including MegaCap Tech.

Lower deficit spending under a Democratic-controlled House could slightly lower long-dated bond yields. A Red Wave could push them higher and could embolden Trump to continue in Iran. Democrats could pull Iran funding or enforce troop removal after 90 days without Congressional approval, but only after the new Congress is seated in January.
Early voting is up sharply, with 43mm votes cast as of Oct 30, about 10mm more than in 2022. Polls from CNBC and Fox now show corruption as the top voting issue, ahead of affordability.

Seasonality: the SPX has been up a year after every midterm since 1950, averaging around 15%. After midterms the SPX has averaged +5.4% over 3 months, 11.4% over 6 months, 12.5% over 9 months and 14.7% over 12 months. The 6, 9 and 12 month returns have a 100% hit rate since 1990. November is the strongest month on average this century.

JPM stays Tactically Bullish. Its Positioning Intel team finds that when the NDX is within about 6% of its all-time high and falls 3.5% or more, it tends to rebound about 3% the following week. The effect is stronger when the decline falls on a Friday, which points to de-grossing rather than a change in fundamentals.

JPM argues the AI capex slowdown is unlikely to cause a recession. Its reasons are record household net worth and cash, record or near-record corporate margins, and AI not being a significant driver of hiring. It sees the main effects as capex declines and possible hyperscaler layoffs rather than an economy-wide shock.

The biggest non-AI risk is a Middle East re-escalation. A WSJ report describes considerable Iranian damage to US regional bases, and munitions are depleted. JPM thinks oil already prices another round of attacks, which limits upside for energy, bond yields and downside for equities.

Updated Monetization Menu (Nov 2): a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals weighted toward Cyclicals. Consumers and Financials can keep working if the curve steepens. Europe could catch a bid if the US and Iran move toward a deal and Value returns.

TMT desk (Brian Heavey): supportive flows in AMZN and GOOGL, with MSFT the main source of funds despite being the cleanest print last week. Financing is the competitive moat, so names that can tap bond markets (GOOGL) are strong and Neoclouds (CRWV, NBIS) keep selling off. SMH reclaimed its 200-day average while shorts are being pressed on elevated volume, and shorts are engaging CPU-linked plays after INTC's drop last week.

Security software is under pressure again, with CHKP the latest negative earnings data point and long selling across the group. OKTA fell on S&P 500 migration, with 1.7m shares for sale effective 11/14.

Financials desk (Taylor Barry): a buy-everything day in Fins as equities catch up to the rate move. Desk volumes were down 23% vs the 5-day average, and moves look driven by pod unwinds and quant de-grossing. Heavily shorted or underweight subsectors acted well, including M&A advisors (EVR, HLI, LAZ), Payments (TOST, AFRM) and Alternative Asset Managers (OWL, STEP).

Energy desk (Brendan Henrici): JPM sees Brent fair value at $94 a barrel, so even at $104 about $10 of risk premium remains. Managed money net long in Brent is about 250mm barrels, below the post-Iran peak but 150mm above the June low and about 20% above the post-2020 average. The CTA position in Brent and WTI is firmly long.

Healthcare desk (Jackie Bukzin): last week's moves looked machine driven and systematic. There was generalist rotation into pharma (MRK), covers in AI-levered names (TWST, TXG) and dedicated funds adding to biotech longs. Managed care shows a preference for Medicaid exposure (better buyer of CNC). Medtech is HF driven, with better selling in SYK and shorts in BAX.

YUM reports Tuesday at 7am ET with a call at 8am. Positioning is mixed to positive. The Street expects about +2% Q4 comps, and buyside expectations for Taco Bell are below the Street at down 4-5% against the Street's -2.4%. Bulls look through the cyclospora headlines and want QTD trends back to flat or positive.

Europe closed higher on a beta-led rally (SX5E +0.7%, DAX +0.6%, SXXP +0.4%, UKX +0.3%). Cyclicals and Quality led while Growth and Momentum lagged. Baskets up 2z or more included UKR Ceasefire and Consumer Recovery, while MidEast Escalation Longs, Higher Gas Winners and Oil Sensitive Energy fell 2z or more.

Calendar: JOLTS, Factory Orders and the US midterm election on Nov 3, with poll closes from 7pm to 1am ET. ADP, ISM Services and the Treasury quarterly refunding announcement on Nov 4. NFP on Nov 6. Heavy earnings Nov 3 to Nov 5 include AMD, AMGN, ANET, BKNG, SMCI, PFE, UBER, QCOM and ABNB. The Fed meeting is Dec 9.

market_movers.rationale: Reports Nov 3 before the open. Positioning is mixed to positive on Taco Bell strength after the Pizza Hut sale, and bulls are looking through cyclospora headlines. Buyside Taco Bell expectations of down 4-5% sit below the Street's -2.4%.
S&P 500 migration implies 1.7m shares for sale effective 11/14, and the stock was hit on the news.
The latest negative earnings data point for security software. The TMT desk notes CHKP has been a short in the space and sees long selling across security names.

sector_views.rationale: Monetization Menu favors a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals with a heavier Cyclicals weight, and Consumers and Financials can work if the yield curve steepens.
JPM thinks Tech was oversold and would play for a tactical rebound, but has not seen the all clear for AI and Tech. It expects the market to become more selective between AI winners and losers.
Constructive on consumer resilience and limited direct AI exposure. The Fins desk sees a buy-everything day with falling rates and a steeper curve helping.
Oil still carries about $10 of risk premium over JPM's $94 Brent fair value, and the Oct 26 menu suggested long oil and Energy equities only as a hedge.
Europe could catch a bid if the US and Iran move toward a deal and Value returns. US Value gained 7.4%, SXXP 7.6% and UKX 9.7% in Jan to Feb.

earnings_insights: AAPL fell about 1.5% after its report on Nov 2 (reported after the close of the prior session per the afternoon update). No EPS figures are given.
MSFT is described by the TMT desk as the cleanest print last week, yet it was the source of funds for AMZN and GOOGL flows.
INTC had a large drop last week after its report, and shorts are now engaging CPU-linked plays.
CHKP reported a negative earnings data point for security software, and the group saw long selling.
YUM reports Nov 3 before the open. Street consensus is about +2% Q4 comps and +5% FY27 Taco Bell comps. Buyside expects Taco Bell comps down 4-5% against the Street's -2.4%, with KFC in line at +2%.
Earnings Nov 3 before the open include ADM, APO, FISV, KDP, MPC, PFE, YUM. After the close: AIG, ALAB, AMD, AMGN, ANET, BKNG, SMCI, SWKS, TOST, XYZ.
Earnings Nov 4 include MCD, UBER, DDOG, CVS, CRCL, MARA before the open and QCOM, SNAP, HUBS, APP, ALB, FICO after. Nov 5 includes COP, SO, ZTS before the open and ABNB, AFRM, DKNG, NET, MCHP after.
The macro read-through from earnings in the brief headline is mixed labor market color (wage inflation, headcount reduction, skilled labor shortages) and bullish comments on AI infrastructure.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest since November 2021 and consistent with solid factory output growth.
Demand is holding up. JPM notes new orders came in above expectations and rose month over month.

macro_indicators.indicator: S&P Global Manufacturing PMI New Orders

macro_indicators.interpretation: Edged down but remains near the highest level of the past few years. PMI employment growth was the strongest in nearly six years.
Supply chain pressure remains elevated. The PMI measure lengthened the most since August 2022.

macro_indicators.reading: pulled back modestly, seasonally adjusted around its second-highest level since March 2022
macro_indicators.interpretation: Input inflation pressure is still high. The PMI input cost inflation reached its highest since May and output price inflation its strongest since September 2022.
Treasury cut its fourth-quarter borrowing estimate, per the Reuters headline in the news links.
JPM's commodity strategist sees fair value $94, implying roughly $10 of risk premium with Brent near $104.

trade_ideas.description: Barbell of Tech and Cyclicals with a heavier weight on Cyclicals (Consumers and Financials), keeping a tactical Tech rebound
trade_ideas.rationale: Broadening can continue as in Jan to Feb but with less Energy appreciation and less Tech downside, especially if the yield curve keeps steepening.
trade_ideas.risk: The market may become increasingly selective between AI winners and losers, and AI headlines on capital raising, circular financing and legal issues may give investors pause.

trade_ideas.description: Add hedges via long oil, Energy equities and long vol (Oct 26 Monetization Menu, retained as a hedge)
trade_ideas.rationale: The prior menu aligns with JPM's view and hedges a Middle East re-escalation.

trade_ideas.description: Long Europe equities if the US and Iran move toward a deal and Value returns
trade_ideas.rationale: In Jan to Feb, US Value gained 7.4%, SXXP 7.6% and UKX 9.7%.

risk_factors: Re-escalation in the Middle East is the biggest non-AI risk.
AI monetization doubts, including headlines on capital raising, circular financing and legal issues, and Neocloud financing stress.
Possible de-grossing within the AI theme if midterm outcomes increase liquidity.
Investigation risk for business leaders tied to Trump donations, including MegaCap Tech.
Elevated inflation and supply-chain pressure from tariffs, energy prices and Middle East disruption.
Positioning in oil is creeping higher, with roughly $10 of risk premium over fair value.
Budget fights and possible government shutdown in a split Congress, with a funding deadline Dec 11.
ECB flagged AI valuations, bond stress and fund losses as main risks (Reuters headline).
vol_and_positioning: A CNBC headline notes the VIX is doing something strange, with no details given in the brief.
Friday's NDX flush of 3.5% or more looks like de-grossing, and historically NDX near its high rebounds about 3% the following week, more so when the decline falls on a Friday.
SMH reclaimed its 200-day average, with shorts being pressed on elevated volume.
The RSP over QQQ trade is up 13% since the selloff began on Oct 7, as Tech money funds other sectors.

Fins desk sees pod unwinds and quant de-grossing driving moves, with desk volumes down 23% vs the 5-day average. Heavily shorted or underweight Fins subsectors are acting well, consistent with hedge fund short unwinds.

Managed money net long in Brent is about 250mm barrels, up about 150mm from the June low and about 20% above the post-2020 average. CTA positioning in Brent and WTI is firmly long, up from moderately long in late September. The commodity team screens Brent at about 5 on a 1-10 score, which never exceeded 8 in 2026.
JPM's Oct 26 Monetization Menu suggested adding hedges via long oil, Energy equities and long vol.
geopolitical: US/Iran deal optimism pushed oil and yields lower. Trump told reporters there are no plans to strike Iran after the elections.
Iran's Khamenei gave the government powers to hold talks on the war (BBG headline).

A WSJ article describes considerable damage inflicted by Iran on US regional bases. Combined with depleted munition levels, JPM thinks another wave of attacks could be limited in scope and duration and may point to heightened diplomatic efforts.
America's Gulf Allies are preparing for a new round of strikes on Iran and the blowback (WSJ headline).
Democrats could pull funding or force removal of US troops engaged in Iran beyond 90 days without Congressional approval, but the timing would be after the new Congress is seated in January.
A Red Wave could embolden Trump to continue in Iran until a US-friendly deal or Iranian capitulation is achieved.
US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027 (NBC). APEC Leaders Meeting is Nov 18-19 in Shenzhen.
The US is pushing to restore Russian gas sales to Europe via Ukraine (WSJ headline). The UKR Ceasefire basket rose 2z in Europe.
US midterm elections on Nov 3, and a US government funding deadline on Dec 11.

tension_points.bull_case: A Blue Wave is unlikely to produce AI-limiting policy because Trump has said he will not sign bills that limit AI expansion and Democrats cannot reach a veto-proof majority. JPM sees any dip as a buying opportunity.
tension_points.bear_case: Many investors fear an AI selloff on assumed higher regulation. Investigation risk for business leaders tied to Trump donations, including MegaCap Tech, and de-grossing within the AI theme on higher assumed liquidity are the risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The market uses the assumed increase in liquidity after a Blue Wave to de-gross within the AI theme.

tension_points.bull_case: Friday's flush tends to be followed by a rebound of about 3%, the broadening trend is strengthening, Tech is stabilizing, data can ease stagflation fears and November plus post-midterm seasonality are tailwinds.
tension_points.bear_case: October was a challenging environment with residual headwinds. AI headlines on capital raising, circular financing and legal issues may give investors pause, and JPM has not yet seen the all clear for AI and Tech.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning has crept higher and a Middle East re-escalation could lift oil again. Brent managed money is about 20% above the post-2020 average.
tension_points.bear_case: JPM sees Brent fair value at $94 versus about $104, so $10 of risk premium remains, and oil markets already appear to price another round of attacks, limiting upside for energy and bond yields.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another series of attacks that proves more damaging than oil already prices, or a US/Iran deal that removes the remaining risk premium.

theme_stances.key_argument: A Friday flush near highs tends to be followed by a rebound, and broadening plus Tech stabilization should push the SPX higher.
theme_stances.evidence: we are sticking with the view.

theme_stances.evidence: We think broadening can continue from here

theme_stances.evidence: even at $104 there is still ~$10 of risk premium in the price
